title: Self-Hosted Serving Selection — llama.cpp, Ollama, TGI, vLLM, SGLang

questions.question: Three engineers propose Ollama, vLLM, and TGI for the same project and all sound right. How do you decide?
options: Decide by hardware first, then scale, then workload
questions.explanation: Every engine wins a different context. This lesson walks the choice tree: hardware, scale, workload — in that order.

questions.question: For AMD production serving of ordinary chat, which engine does the decision tree select?
options: TGI, because it is the only maintained option
Ollama, because production always uses the dev wrapper
questions.explanation: The AMD branch starts with vLLM; only agentic or prefix-heavy workloads switch to SGLang. TRT-LLM is NVIDIA-locked in the lesson.

questions.question: What does the tree choose for NVIDIA Hopper production with an agentic multi-turn workload?
questions.explanation: The Hopper branch checks for agentic or prefix-heavy workload first and selects SGLang, the prefix/agent specialist.

questions.question: What primary engine does NVIDIA Blackwell enterprise serving receive in the supplied MoE scenario?
options: Ollama, because it is faster than all GPU engines
TGI, because it is in active feature development
questions.explanation: The Blackwell branch selects TRT-LLM and the enterprise scale branch adds the Phase 17 production stack, disaggregated serving, and cache-aware router.

questions.question: What maintenance status does the lesson assign to TGI?
options: It is the new default after a February 2026 feature release
It entered maintenance mode on December 11, 2025
It has no release or maintenance policy
questions.explanation: The docs date TGI's maintenance mode to December 11, 2025, which biases new projects toward vLLM or SGLang.

questions.question: What stack does the enterprise branch append to its engine recommendation?
options: A browser WebGPU runtime and mobile NPU
A batch API and a semantic embedding model
questions.explanation: For scale=enterprise, pick_engine adds the exact Phase 17 composition: production-stack, disaggregated serving, and cache-aware routing.
